docs.title: savagecarol
docs.text: Hi, I'm Kartikeya Sharma. I run a YouTube channel called savagecarol where I break down System Design concepts in a simple, practical, and interview-ready way. This website is the written companion to that channel — clean Markdown guides, no fluff.

docs.title: The irony
docs.text: I talk about large-scale distributed systems... but this entire site is a simple static site built with MkDocs and hosted on GitHub Pages. No microservices. No Kubernetes. Just Markdown. Sometimes simple is enough.

docs.title: Help build this
docs.text: I need help writing Markdown guides on the system design topics I teach. If you contribute even one topic, you help thousands of developers learn. I will review and merge every contribution.

docs.title: Links
docs.text:
▶️ YouTube — watch the videos

🐙 GitHub — contribute Markdown guides

💼 LinkedIn — connect with me

docs.title: Redis
docs.text: Video Explanation: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gaedF2RpJ7A&list=PL4gQGtQMQlFX3lpLT40wE2lWCQpdXedd5

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Redis is an in-memory key-value data store widely used for caching, session storage, rate limiting, and pub/sub messaging. It provides extremely low latency and high throughput, making it useful for scalable distributed systems.

docs.title: gRPC
docs.text: Video Explanation: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=snZnPv2u72I&list=PL4gQGtQMQlFWWprCkOJvg3jz1Z3GXtOU-

docs.title: Description
docs.text: gRPC is a high-performance RPC framework developed by Google. It uses HTTP/2 and Protocol Buffers for fast and efficient communication between services, commonly used in microservices architectures.

docs.title: ZooKeeper
docs.text: Video Explanation: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=65HYnPJ7t14&list=PL4gQGtQMQlFW-d4F7UySNIJT8W-Z0isSr

docs.title: Description
docs.text: ZooKeeper is a distributed coordination service used for configuration management, leader election, and synchronization between services in a distributed system.

docs.title: Kafka
docs.text: Video Explanation: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kAbtgMYtXcY&list=PL4gQGtQMQlFVKbuN_QCcwcGLuoKR5Xg6b

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Apache Kafka is a distributed event streaming platform used for building real-time data pipelines and event-driven systems. It allows services to publish and consume events reliably at large scale.

docs.title: SOLID Principles & Design Patterns – Video Guide
docs.text: A curated list of SOLID principles and common design patterns with short explanations and video resources.

docs.title: 1. What is SOLID Principle
docs.text:
SOLID is a set of five object-oriented design principles that help developers write maintainable, scalable, and loosely coupled software.

Video: https://youtu.be/iVg_IHTw6tU?si=XB-mib0QJTCBSl2n

docs.title: 2. What are Design Patterns (Creational, Structural, Behavioral)
docs.text:
Design patterns are reusable solutions to common software design problems categorized into Creational, Structural, and Behavioral patterns.

Video: https://youtu.be/Cy59bJ3Gk9o?si=8YrnLh1qBWOx9s2l

docs.title: 3. Singleton Pattern
docs.text:
Ensures that a class has only one instance and provides a global access point to it.

Video: https://youtu.be/cDM-DeBX1pw?si=QsNM7rxJcyYpg_aR

docs.title: 4. Factory Method Pattern
docs.text:
Defines an interface for creating objects while letting subclasses decide which class to instantiate.

Video: https://youtu.be/zsDepMauAes?si=Gy7sG_BLG4kcqVeb

docs.title: 5. Abstract Factory Pattern
docs.text:
Provides an interface for creating families of related or dependent objects without specifying their concrete classes.

Video: https://youtu.be/t_QjDIzzCxE?si=q2zKPEBNioEsAOzX

docs.title: 6. Builder Pattern
docs.text:
Separates the construction of a complex object from its representation so the same construction process can create different objects.

Video: https://youtu.be/QIbQbwFODAw?si=cTwJRR02v9r53GLh

docs.title: 7. Prototype Pattern
docs.text:
Creates new objects by copying an existing instance instead of creating a new one from scratch.

Video: https://youtu.be/sc1lUC3AgdI?si=jKWA-deElFh9KZ5h

docs.title: 8. Adapter Pattern
docs.text:
Allows incompatible interfaces to work together by converting one interface into another.

Video: https://youtu.be/DqCqYMw3AVY?si=VtIXen71j1y-ALhs

docs.title: 9. Decorator Pattern
docs.text:
Adds new functionality to objects dynamically without modifying their structure.

Video: https://youtu.be/WxcYvrch1gE?si=jLX-mSyinBAQQir5

docs.title: 10. Facade Pattern
docs.text:
Provides a simplified interface to a complex subsystem.

Video: https://youtu.be/vxRVEb2-0kA?si=5GTh7DUhHRVctOwi

docs.title: 11. Composite Pattern
docs.text:
Composes objects into tree structures to represent part-whole hierarchies.

Video: https://youtu.be/qnexSXUelFs?si=FFVWKpRva3JNNAIA

docs.title: 12. Proxy Pattern
docs.text:
Provides a placeholder object that controls access to another object.

Video: https://youtu.be/d8D4sqTzDaw?si=_YM2Lx49qDKJLczh

docs.title: 13. Bridge Pattern
docs.text:
Decouples an abstraction from its implementation so that both can evolve independently.

Video: https://youtu.be/2cuEHwSGJ9o?si=YE2S6TSNMlvhPis2

docs.title: 14. Flyweight Pattern
docs.text:
Reduces memory usage by sharing common parts of objects instead of creating many similar instances.

Video: https://youtu.be/_CSwCck6cCw?si=d-ViGGG_eo5UO-rm

docs.title: 15. Chain of Responsibility Pattern
docs.text:
Passes a request along a chain of handlers until one of them processes it.

Video: https://youtu.be/TlCtoRS08vM?si=GuKRuGXTqaKpWvO-

docs.title: 16. Observer Pattern
docs.text:
Defines a one-to-many dependency where multiple observers are notified automatically when a subject changes state.

Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_BpmfnqjgzQ

docs.title: 17. Strategy Pattern
docs.text:
Defines a family of algorithms and makes them interchangeable at runtime.

Video: https://youtu.be/d_3IM8Z739c?si=Sr1n0w4ktD-6EUTd

docs.title: 18. Command Pattern
docs.text:
Encapsulates a request as an object, allowing parameterization and queuing of requests.

Video: https://youtu.be/Tw8nW8k5-zc?si=lkxFiLIXk0MWSjrQ

docs.title: 19. State Pattern
docs.text:
Allows an object to change its behavior when its internal state changes.

Video: https://youtu.be/jw13tzKHeoA?si=LzpcpFjjze_Lk_1t

docs.title: 20. Template Method Pattern
docs.text:
Defines the skeleton of an algorithm while allowing subclasses to override certain steps.

Video: https://youtu.be/jw13tzKHeoA?si=9dLwZKlF0hKGbuIh

docs.title: 21. Mediator Pattern
docs.text:
Reduces direct dependencies between objects by making them communicate through a mediator.

Video: https://youtu.be/TlCtoRS08vM?si=RYJeKp5Ih_DxjBdg

docs.title: 22. Iterator Pattern
docs.text:
Provides a way to sequentially access elements of a collection without exposing its underlying representation.

Video: https://youtu.be/wWDDNGSMu68?si=wXxblL1e_ui0ywWK

docs.title: 23. Memento Pattern
docs.text:
Captures and restores an object's internal state without exposing its implementation details.

Video: https://youtu.be/SLP6-69Fb-0?si=Nnez87nealxdfLWL

docs.title: 24. Interpreter Pattern
docs.text:
Defines a grammar for a language and provides an interpreter to evaluate sentences in that language.

Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0L9t4j-0hQ0

docs.title: 25. Visitor Pattern
docs.text:
Separates algorithms from the objects on which they operate so new operations can be added easily.

Video: https://youtu.be/YUkWCGoNPFY?si=RD04643ArBXhPj6g
